title: Nonemptiness of a finite probability space
statement: If a type $\Omega$ carries the structure of a finite probability space — that is, it is finite and discrete, and is equipped with a probability measure — then $\Omega$ is nonempty.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite probability space (finite, discrete measurable space carrying a probability measure)
replaced: Any type carrying a \texttt{FiniteProbabilitySpace} instance is nonempty.
